differences.what: massing: a long, low, one-storey house with its ridge along the river front, the front about two and a half times the gable end
differences.how: T-2509: log_dwelling on a 14.6 x 5.5 m plan with a 2.4 m wall. T-2511 lowered the roof from 30 to 24 degrees, which brings the ridge's right end from y 163.2 px down to the drawing's 167 (the render's ridge now reads at 166)

differences.what: the river front's openings: three doors and six small windows in the order window, door, window, window, door, window, window, door, window
differences.how: T-2511: log_dwelling gained a stated front set-out (front_set_out), and the record gives the nine openings in the plate's order, each centre read off the plate on a 1 px grid and carried onto the wall through this camera. Doors 1.2 m and windows 0.85 x 0.8 m wide as read, bare sash with no shutters as drawn. The heads stand on one line as the plate draws them, but at 1.7 m rather than the drawing's 1.5 m (see the last difference)

differences.what: the stack: the plate stands it outside the LEFT (upstream) gable as seen from the river
differences.how: T-2511: chimney_end 'max' puts it on the upstream gable, and chimney_cross_m slides it to that gable's front corner, which is where this camera puts the drawn stack (x 308-322 px against the drawing's 310-325; centred it stood at 289-302). chimney_head_m holds its head at 3.9 m, at the drawing's y 165 and just clear of the ridge, where the archetype's rule stood it 10 px taller

differences.what: a lower gabled lean-to beyond the stack at the left end, drawn gable-on to the viewer
differences.how: T-2511: lean_to builds a plank shed against the upstream gable behind the stack, its ridge across the house's so its gable faces the river: 2.3 m out, 1.8 m across, a 2.2 m eave and a 45 degree roof. Its gable lands at x 297-313 px against the drawing's 297.5-312, its eave at y 184 against 184, its apex about 171 against 172. Its board door is this project's

differences.what: the walls: the plate draws them smooth and pale with no courses and no notched corners
differences.how: T-2511 ruled whitewash, at the reconstructed tier (log_finish, L-1812-lees-place-2511): the plate draws the lean-to's boards, the fence's rails and the stack's shade where it saw them, so the flat pale wall reads as a coat rather than the wash drawing's shorthand. The logs and chinking are whitewashed together; the notched ends at the corners still show as relief, which the drawing at 2 px a course does not resolve

differences.what: the roof's tone: the plate draws the roof much darker than the walls
differences.how: T-2511: roof_condition 'darkened', the sheet's weather-blackened condition, so the roof now reads darker than the whitewashed walls as the print draws it. The print's near-black is a solid wash; how much darker it means is not a measure a monochrome drawing gives

differences.what: the back wall and the right (downstream) gable
differences.how: The plate sees the front and the left end only

differences.what: the lean-to's upstream side and roof slope show in the render, about 17 px of wall left of its gable; the plate draws the lean-to flat to the viewer with no side
differences.how: Argued unbuildable, not left undone: through this camera any lean-to with depth shows a side here (a ridge along the house instead shows its gable 15-25 px wide and its side between it and the stack), and only a shed under a metre deep could look as the plate draws it. T-2509's solve already records that the lean-to's perspective disagrees with the main roof's and that the two cannot both hold. Narrowed to 1.8 m to keep the side small; the picture is wrong here about any building that could have stood there

differences.what: the door and window heads stand at 1.7 m, about 1-2 px higher than the drawing's 1.5 m
differences.how: Deliberate: the plate's door heads read 1.49-1.54 m over grade through the camera, lower than a person walks under, so the build keeps a low cabin door of 1.7 m and the drawing's single line of heads (L-1812-lees-place-2511)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
note: Reviewed by T-2511 against the side-by-side, element by element: the massing, the nine openings in the plate's order, the stack on the upstream gable and its height, the lean-to, the walls' finish and the roof's tone are each built as the plate shows them. Two differences stay open and are argued rather than built: the lean-to's side, which the drawing's own perspective cannot hold for any lean-to with depth, and the door heads, kept at a height a person can walk under. The plate is a retrospective wash drawing (tier 5) by an unnamed illustrator, about a century after the farm.
